scope: Two Williams specializations in the retained old41 proof; local Selberg algebra and prime-pattern theorem remain separate.

source.statement: For a fixed arithmetic progression with coprime residue and modulus, the Mertens product has a positive constant and the prescribed reciprocal-logarithm exponent. In particular the two unit classes modulo4 have exponent1/2; removing finitely many fixed primes changes only the positive constant.

available.exceptional_cases: Nonreduced residues are not covered by this assertion.
available.limit_order: Fix progression and exclusions before the cutoff tends to infinity.

rows.needed: For fixed m<=41 and Q>2m, product over Q<q<=L of(1−2m/q) is bounded below by a positive fixed constant times(log L)^(-2m).
rows.derivation: Compare log(1−2m/q) with2m log(1−1/q); their difference is O_m(q^-2), whose tail converges. Apply Williams in the unique unit class modulo2; finitely many removed primes affect only a positive Q,m-dependent constant.
rows.boundary: The surviving residue density uses the earlier union bound; the asymptotic X threshold may still depend on L.

rows.needed: The two Euler products have respectively growth log z for split primes with rho=2q−1, and(log z)^(m−1) for all primes with rho=(m−1)q; the displayed truncation yields the same lower orders for G(Z).
rows.derivation: Expand log(1+h(q)) to first order. Williams modulo4 gives exponent2*(1/2)=1 in the norm sieve; modulo2 gives m−1 in the other sieve. The O(q^-2) errors converge. Use z=Z^(1/512) and the local weighted-log expectation bound to retain at least half the mass belowZ. Omitting one supported q loses at most a factor2 by the displayed h(q) formula and fixed lower cutoff.
rows.boundary: Williams supplies the prime product, not the Selberg identity or truncation probability argument; those are explicit local computations. Constants depend on fixedQ,m but not the omitted prime.
